Widespread tree damage occurred in a corridor from northeast Bexar County through central San Antonio into southwest Bexar County. Scattered damage to fences, power lines, and power poles has also occurred, along with some damage to roofs. At the peak, over 104,000 customers were without power. The damage is consistent with straight-line winds. Measured wind speeds reached 50-65 mph, with pockets of 75 mph winds estimated from radar and the resulting damage.

*** 1 FATAL *** Two people were in a drainage area during heavy rainfall when they were swept downstream. One person escaped while another drowned, with police and fire crew recovering the body at San Pedro Creek near West Quincy Street. Time is estimated.

Preliminary results from an NWS ground survey and supplemental footage from TDEM and Bexar OEM concluded strong downdraft winds with speeds up to around 75 mph caused intermittent damage to trees and fences in Kirby mainly south of Binz Engleman Road. Damage included medium to large tree branches snapped, several downed fences, and a few locations with sheet metal damage on structures. The most concentrated area of damage was near James Webb Drive where a carport roof was displaced.

*** 1 FATAL *** A flash flood fatality occurred in San Pedro Creek, near Furnish Avenue and South San Marcos. The investigation is still ongoing into the flash flood fatality, but it was not believed to be vehicle related.

*** 1 FATAL *** Heavy rainfall occurred Monday and Monday night across the northeast side of San Antonio. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain occurred. This caused a quick rise into flood stage on Salado Creek early Tuesday morning. One flash flood fatality occurred within the Salado Creek Greenway, near J Street Park.

*** 11 FATAL, 4 INJ *** Corrects previous flash flood report from 2 WSW Windcrest. Updated fatality count from previous flash flood report. Training of thunderstorms with intense rainfall rates occurred across the region. A swath of 3-8 inches of rain was measured. At least 15 vehicles were swept into Beitel Creek near Loop 410 and Perrin Beitel Road area. There are at least 11 confirmed fatalities in this creek and/or in nearby portions of San Antonio and unknown number of unaccounted for at the time of this new update. Ten people were rescued and two others were able to get to safety on their own.

A non-vehicle related flash flood fatality was reported near Wurzbach Parkway and Salado Creek on June 14th associated with the flooding from June 12th. Time of LSR is estimated based on radar and previous storm reports. Exact location unknown.
